subject.title: fix(security): avoid false-positive secret findings when config uses env references

question: Should the security audit rely on the new optional `ConfigFileSnapshot.includedSourceConfig` contract to suppress findings for externally supplied environment references?
rationale: The implementation and proof are strong, but approving a new snapshot contract and intentionally suppressing security findings are ownership decisions that automated review should not make alone.

options.title: Approve the provenance contract
options.body: Accept the optional snapshot field and the tested rule that only references not backed by `env.NAME` or `env.vars.NAME` suppress stored-secret findings.

options.title: Keep provenance audit-private
options.body: Preserve the same behavior but refactor the pre-substitution view into an internal config-audit result instead of extending `ConfigFileSnapshot`.

recommendation.title: Approve the provenance contract
recommendation.body: Accept the optional snapshot field and the tested rule that only references not backed by `env.NAME` or `env.vars.NAME` suppress stored-secret findings.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice primarily governs core security-audit classification and the long-term ownership boundary for sensitive config provenance.
